title: CI deploy orchestration contract and audit playbook
author: Marisol Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines the formal deployment orchestration contract for Redwood Inference CI pipelines, plus the operational playbook and audit taxonomy required for production-safe rollouts. The goal is to standardize how services and model artifacts progress from build -> staging -> canary -> prod, how gates are evaluated, what events are auditable, and who owns each step.

Intended audience:
- Platform engineers who operate the CI/CD system
- Service owners and release engineers performing rollouts
- Security & compliance reviewers and auditors

Scope and principles:
1) Single source of truth for promotion: every promotion must be driven by a signed artifact and an immutable promotion record stored in the deployment ledger.
2) Gate-first rollouts: automated quality gates (tests, telemetry, canary metrics) must pass before manual/automated promotion.
3) Auditable by design: every pipeline run emits structured audit events ingested into the central logging cluster and retained for 365 days.
4) Minimal blast radius: default canary size = 5% traffic, max 25% without explicit owner approval.
5) Reproducibility: every deploy is reproducible from the build id and container image digest.

Contract: deployment orchestration API and required fields
The CI/CD orchestration layer provides a REST API and a CLI wrapper. All promotions must supply the following canonical fields (ledger record):
- build_id: unique build number (string)
- artifact_digest: sha256://... (container or model artifact digest)
- artifact_signature: cosign signature base64 (or key-id)
- target_env: staging|canary|production
- release_notes_id: internal doc id or changelog URL
- owner: team-name or service-owner (email)
- rollout_policy: immediate|gradual|manual
- canary_config: stringified JSON (see example)
- required_gates: list of gate ids (unit-tests, integration-tests, telemetry-sli, security-scan)
- correlation_id: UUID for end-to-end tracing

Sample ledger JSON (stored as an immutable record):
{
  "build_id": "20250912-817",
  "artifact_digest": "sha256:3b9a...f8b",
  "artifact_signature": "cosign:ci-key-1:BASE64SIG==",
  "target_env": "canary",
  "release_notes_id": "RN-3421",
  "owner": "incorporation-service-team@redwood.com",
  "rollout_policy": "gradual",
  "canary_config": "{\"traffic_percent\":5,\"duration_minutes\":30}",
  "required_gates": ["unit-tests", "integration-tests", "telemetry-sli", "security-scan"],
  "correlation_id": "b7a9d4c6-..."
}

Gate definitions and enforcement matrix
| Gate id | What is checked | Enforcement action | Owner |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------|-------|
| unit-tests | CI job pass (exit 0) and coverage threshold >= 80% for critical packages | block promotion | service owner (CI job) |
| integration-tests | end-to-end tests against staging fixtures (including model smoke) | block promotion | release engineer |
| telemetry-sli | canary metrics for latency (p50/p95), errors, and correctness evals | block or auto-rollforward with approval | platform SRE |
| security-scan | SCA scan, container CVE threshold (no critical), binary signing present | block and open ticket | security team |
| data-provenance | model artifact has provenance metadata and lineage | block | model-onboarding team |

Required thresholds (default):
- Latency p95 increase vs baseline <= 15%
- Error rate increase <= 0.5 percentage points OR absolute error rate <= 0.5%
- Regression in eval accuracy <= 1% relative drop on canary prompt set

Canary orchestration playbook (gradual rollout)
1) Start canary (CI command): redwood-ci promote --build $BUILD_ID --target canary --policy gradual --canary 5 --duration 30m
2) Platform creates canary slice and routes 5% production traffic to canary variant. Canary telemetry is tagged with correlation_id and canary=true.
3) Wait for warmup period: 3 minutes for cold-start stabilization, then monitor for duration window: 30 minutes.
4) Evaluate automated gates: telemetry-sli and correctness evals run in background. If gates pass, automatically scale to 25% over an owner-defined step schedule, otherwise trigger rollback.
5) Final approval: once at 25% for 60 minutes with gates green, CI promotions may progress to production if rollout_policy allows. Otherwise, manual approval required.

Failure modes and immediate actions
- Telemetry anomaly (exceeded latency/error thresholds): pause rollout, revert traffic to baseline, notify oncall, create investigation ticket with tags: deploy-failure, canary, service-name.
- Security scan failure discovered post-promotion: immediate quarantine of artifact, block further promotions using that artifact digest, notify security and product owners, and start incident review per incident process.
- Stalled promotion (operator stuck > 120 minutes): auto-escalate to oncall and send digest to paging channel.

Rollback procedure (fast path)
1) Execute: redwood-ci rollback --artifact-digest sha256:... --env production --reason "telemetry-regression"
2) Orchestrator switches route table to previous stable digest using atomic flip; validate health checks for 2 minutes.
3) Emit audit event: deploy.rollback with correlation_id, failing_gate, initiator.
4) Open postmortem ticket and assign owner from ledger owner field.

Audit event taxonomy (structured events emitted by pipeline):
- deploy.requested
- deploy.candidate.validated
- deploy.canary.started
- deploy.canary.metric_snapshot (p50/p95/error/accuracy)
- deploy.canary.decision (pass|fail|escalate)
- deploy.promoted
- deploy.rollback
- deploy.quarantine (security)
- deploy.signing.verification
Each event MUST include: timestamp ISO8601, build_id, artifact_digest, correlation_id, initiator, target_env, and optional details (reason, metric snapshot).

Retention and access
- Audit event retention: 365 days in central logstore (write-once).
- Audit view: read-only dashboards for compliance and security reviewers; access controlled via RBAC.
- Export format: JSONL with event types documented above.

SLOs and operational objectives for the orchestration subsystem
- Deploy success rate (from canary start to prod without rollback): 99% monthly.
- Mean time to promote (canary->prod for gradual policy): P50 < 45 minutes, P95 < 180 minutes.
- Time to rollback (fast path): P50 < 3 minutes, P95 < 10 minutes.
- Ledger write latency: 99% < 250ms for promotion record writes.

Ownership and responsibilities
- CI platform team: implement orchestration API, ledger storage, audit emission, RBAC enforcement, and canary plumbing.
- Service owner: provide release notes, review gate failures, and accept the final promotion.
- SRE: maintain telemetry SLOs and run housekeeping for canary traffic routing.
- Security: define scanning thresholds and key management for signing.

Tooling and example commands
- Build + sign artifact (container):
  docker build -t registry.redwood.com/incorp:20250912-817 .
  docker push registry.redwood.com/incorp@sha256:3b9a...f8b
  cosign sign --key ksm://projects/ci/cosign-key registry.redwood.com/incorp@sha256:3b9a...f8b

- Promote to canary (CLI):
  redwood-ci promote --build 20250912-817 --digest sha256:3b9a...f8b --target canary --canary 5 --duration 30m --correlation b7a9d4c6-...

- Rollback (CLI):
  redwood-ci rollback --artifact-digest sha256:previousStable --env production --reason 'p95-latency-regression' --correlation b7a9d4c6-...

Sample CI pipeline job (YAML snippet):

pipeline:
  stages:
    - name: build-and-sign
      image: docker:stable
      script:
        - make build
        - docker push $IMAGE
        - cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY $IMAGE
    - name: promote
      image: redwood/ci-agent:latest
      script:
        - redwood-ci validate --build $BUILD_ID --gates unit-tests,integration-tests,security-scan
        - redwood-ci promote --build $BUILD_ID --digest $ARTIFACT_DIGEST --target canary --canary 5 --duration 30m

Checklist before a manual production promotion
1) Artifact signed and ledger entry exists.
2) All required gates green for the canary window.
3) Runbook URL and post-deploy contact listed in release_notes.
4) Observability dashboard pre-saved with correlation filtering.
5) Approval from service owner (email/approver id).

Metrics to populate dashboards
- deploy.attempts (per service, per day)
- deploy.successes
- deploy.rollbacks
- deploy.ledger.write_latency_ms
- canary.p95_latency_delta
- canary.error_rate_delta
- artifact.signature_verification_failures

Escalation and oncall flow
1) Automatic alert if telemetry-sli gate fails: page SRE oncall and post message to #deployments with correlation_id.
2) If the rollout is > 120 minutes without decision, page release-engineer oncall.
3) For security quarantine, page security response team and create high-priority ticket.

Testing and staging guidance
- Every service MUST include a synthetic canary job that runs the canonical canary prompt set against the model/service in staging and reports expected correctness metrics to the telemetry SLI system before promotion.
- Periodic chaos exercises: run one simulated-canary-failure game-day per quarter to validate rollback paths and telemetry coverage.

Appendix: sample telemetry SLI snapshot (JSON example)
{
  "p50_latency_ms": 23.4,
  "p95_latency_ms": 81.2,
  "error_rate": 0.003,
  "accuracy_eval": 0.912,
  "baseline_p95_latency_ms": 70.2
}
